nodes.claim: n >= 3, real kappa >= 4, and any actual O in full O(n).
A is symmetric and ||v||^2 <= v^T A v <= kappa ||v||^2 for all coordinate v. Derive via ||Ov||=||v||, |<v,Ov>|<=||v||^2 and the nonnegative coefficient kappa-1.
The source's single-block law is N(0,A^-1); Appendix p_O denotes its density relative to dx.

The canonical coordinate map WithLp.ofLp identifies EuclideanSpace Real (Fin n) isometrically with R^n, sends its volume to product scalar Lebesgue volume, and identifies squared norm with sum of squares and matrix quadratic forms with coordinate dot products.
For the literal source precision A_O, v != 0 implies v^T A_O v >= ||v||^2 > 0, and A_O is symmetric. Produce A_O.PosDef internally for the shared theorem call; it is not a source-theorem hypothesis.

For the general provider, take any n : Nat and A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) Real with hA : A.PosDef. This background theorem includes dimension zero and has no source-specific n, kappa or O restriction.

From the general domain hA, A is real symmetric positive definite, det A > 0 and A is invertible; its matrix inverse is the genuine inverse, not the total singular fallback. In dimension zero the empty determinant is 1 and these conclusions remain valid.
C=A^-1 is real symmetric positive definite, AC=CA=I, C^-1=A, and det C=(det A)^-1 > 0.
S=CFC.sqrt C is the real symmetric positive definite square root, S*S=C. It is invertible with positive determinant, and (S^-1)^T*S^-1=C^-1=A.

stdGaussian E is the pushforward of independent scalar standard gaussianReal coordinates through the canonical orthonormal coordinate isometry. This is the existing constructor, with no new surrogate law.

Scalar standard Gaussian has Lebesgue density (2*pi)^(-1/2) exp(-t^2/2); finite products and the canonical coordinate isometry give stdGaussian E = volume.withDensity (ofReal ((2*pi)^(-(n:Real)/2) * exp(-||y||^2/2))). This actual standard Gaussian density must be established or reused explicitly.

For zero mean and covariance C, the existing multivariateGaussian is (stdGaussian E).map L, where L=Matrix.toEuclideanCLM S. The zero translation simplifies literally; the covariance parameter is the genuine C from B2. This is general standard background independent of the paper's O-family.

nodes.kind: standard linear coordinate and determinant background
nodes.claim: L is the continuous linear equivalence represented by S in the canonical orthonormal coordinates. Its determinant equals det S. Its inverse is represented by S^-1.

For this invertible L, pushforward of volume.withDensity f is volume.withDensity (x -> (ofReal (1/abs(det S))) * f(L^-1 x)). This is the genuine absolute-Jacobian formula on actual Euclidean volume, with map measurability and inverse conditions proved internally.
For every x, ||L^-1 x||^2 = (coord x)^T (S^-1)^T S^-1 (coord x) = (coord x) dot (A * coord x), including x=0.
det S>0 and (det S)^2=det C=(det A)^-1 imply 1/abs(det S)=sqrt(det A). No orientation restriction on O is used.

Since 2*pi>0 and det A>0, (2*pi)^(-(n:Real)/2)=1/(2*pi)^((n:Real)/2). The product scalar normalizer has this exact real exponent. All real density factors are finite and nonnegative; ofReal products and quotients simplify to the exact single ofReal expression. The density is continuous and measurable.
Expanding B6, inserting the actual standard density B5 and applying B8 gives the canonical law as withDensity of the transformed standard density times the true inverse absolute Jacobian.

When n=0, empty determinant=1, quadratic=0 and real exponent n/2=0. The canonical Gaussian and actual Euclidean volume both have mass one on the singleton; the displayed density is one. The inverse square-root linear map is the unique equivalence of the singleton, with determinant one. No positive-dimension restriction is needed.
